title: SLA-driven gating and evaluation rubric for bespoke billing & commitment proposals
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and channel partners request bespoke commitments, marketplace credits, or invoicing exceptions at unpredictable cadence. Current handling is ad-hoc across sales, finance, and support which increases approval time, creates inconsistent financial outcomes, and surfaces untracked edge cases.

Goal: Define a standardized gating process and evaluation rubric that (1) routes requests by expected financial and operational impact, (2) provides clear SLA targets for review and decision, (3) prescribes finance/legal/ops guardrails (caps, offsets, contract language), and (4) enables automated scoring and a small set of deterministic outcomes to speed approvals and reduce managerial churn.
acceptance_criteria: An intake form template in Salesforce/Notion with fields required by the rubric is published
Automated score (low|medium|high impact) computed from intake fields and visible to reviewers
SLA bands defined: 48h review for SLA-1, 5 business days for SLA-2, 10 business days for SLA-3
Finance-approved cap table and discount tiers linked to score outcomes
Playbook includes explicit marketplace-credit handling and invoicing flow for each outcome
success_metrics: Median time-to-decision for bespoke billing requests reduced from current baseline to <= 3 business days
>90% of requests resolved without ad-hoc exec sign-off
Reduction in revenue leakage from undocumented offsets to < 0.5% of monthly committed revenue
proposed_flow: 1) Intake: sales or partner fills standardized form capturing ARR impact, term, customer tier, compliance flags, marketplace involvement, and requested concession type
2) Automated scoring: system computes impact score using rubric (ARR, strategic label, legal risk, product scope) and assigns SLA band
3) Queue & notification: request appears in Billing Review queue with SLA countdown and suggested outcome
4) Review: Revenue Ops + Finance perform verification; Legal reviews only for SLA-1 or flagged contract changes
5) Decision: Approve (auto-generate amendment/invoice), Approve-with-conditions (cap + follow-up), Decline (standard template + upsell path), Escalate-to-exec (rare, requires justification)
6) Post-decision: record structured outcome, update billing system, and notify customer + Sales
scoring_rubric: Contract complexity: new T&Cs or data residency = +2 points
Marketplace involvement: requests that require marketplace credit orchestration = +1 point
Legal/Compliance flags: PII/Security concerns = automatic SLA-1
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (pilot): route all EMEA bespoke billing requests through the rubric for 6 weeks
Phase 2: enable automated scoring and SLA timers in Zendesk/Notion and integrate with Finance approval workflow
Phase 3: expand to Marketplace partner requests and add marketplace-credit offset automation
Training: 1-hour cross-functional training and recorded walkthrough for Sales + RevOps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict caps drive churn. Mitigation: allow one-time exec exceptions and track reasons to refine caps
Risk: Intake data quality (sales skip fields). Mitigation: make key fields required and validate via automated checks before queueing
Risk: Legal reviews create bottleneck. Mitigation: only SLA-1 auto-requires Legal; provide templated contract clauses to expedite review
Risk: Marketplace bookkeeping complexity. Mitigation: build a small service to model credit offsets and reconcile monthly with Marketplace ops
notes: This approach deliberately favors deterministic outcomes and minimal free-text decisions to scale approvals
Finance requested an initial cap table that scales with term length and up-front payment — see Drive spreadsheet
Consider later adding ML-assisted scoring to surface anomalous requests that appear low-score but high-risk
